mechanism_narrative: A decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility from 18.9 to 15.6 over the last two weeks signals residents spending less time at home, which increases out-of-home retail and recreation footfall and raises RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 18.9 at t-1w to 15.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains below 16 for the next two weeks while the 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its trailing 28-day mean, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT crosses above -55 percent change from baseline, commuter and visitor volumes recover enough to lift weekday retail footfall, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -55 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -62.0 at t-1w to -55.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT exceeds -55 for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC's next 14-day mean is not higher than its previous 14-day mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: The joint recovery of WORKPLACES and TRANSIT above their recent troughs indicates restored commuting and office-adjacent spending; this interaction lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -56.3 at t-1w to -47.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: If both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT meet the trigger thresholds but RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean does not exceed its trailing 28-day mean, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Under a vaccine-expansion reopening regime, falling GROCERY_PHARM stockpiling (less negative) frees household time and spending for discretionary retail, raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -14.1 at t-1w to -8.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM becomes less negative while RETAIL_REC's next 14-day mean is not higher than its previous 14-day mean, the regime-conditional claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: As PARKS mobility falls below 30 percent above baseline from its t-2w peak, outdoor substitution weakens and indoor retail demand recovers, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean falls below 30 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 46.0 at t-2w to 22.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS stays below 30 while RETAIL_REC's next 14-day mean is not higher than its previous 14-day mean, the substitution mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of declining RESIDENTIAL and improving GROCERY_PHARM indicates a shift from home-centered to out-of-home routines, which raises RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 15.6 and GROCERY_PHARM was -8.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If both proxies satisfy the trigger but RETAIL_REC's next 14-day mean does not exceed its previous 14-day mean, the interaction is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC's own upward momentum from -62.1 at t-1w to -50.3 at t-0w signals a regime shift in retail mobility; this momentum carries forward and raises the next four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose 11.8 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: If after a week-on-week RETAIL_REC rise greater than 10 points, the next 28-day mean is not higher than the trailing 28-day mean, momentum fails.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM improves above -10 and PARKS falls below 25, households shift from outdoor and grocery-focused trips to discretionary retail, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM was -8.6 and PARKS was 22.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: If both conditions hold but RETAIL_REC's next 7-day mean does not exceed its previous 7-day mean, the shift mechanism is rejected.
